title: ZYFA: Speed and Accuracy of FP8 FlashAttention on AMD CDNA4
abstract: Attention is a core building block of frontier models and often dominates compute-bound prefill at long context. FP8 matrix instructions offer twice the peak throughput of BF16, but they accelerate only matrix multiplication, and the softmax between the two matrix multiplications of attention runs on vector units that FP8 does not accelerate. On the AMD Instinct MI355X, the vendor's AITER kernels reach 39% of peak FP8 matrix throughput at 32K tokens, compared with 49% in BF16. Attention is also more numerically sensitive to quantization than feed-forward layers, and unlike NVIDIA's Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, the MI355X does not track the completion of matrix instructions in hardware, so overlapping the softmax with the matrix multiplications depends on instruction order. We present ZYFA, prefill kernels for the MI355X built on three techniques: (1) computing each FP8 probability directly from its score with a multiply-add and an integer conversion instead of an exponential; (2) a ping-pong schedule in which one group of threads computes its softmax while another executes its matrix multiplications; and (3) scaling each block of probabilities up by a power of two before rounding, and normalizing by the sum of the rounded probabilities. On attention inputs captured from three models and timed at sustained clock speeds, ZYFA achieves 1.16-1.76x the throughput of AITER. On the Gaussian inputs of kernel benchmarks at 32K tokens, it achieves 1.26-1.37x at head dimension 128 and 1.99x for DeepSeek-style multi-head latent attention. The sustained clock of the MI355X depends on operand values, so throughput on random inputs does not reliably predict throughput on real model activations. At head dimension 128, ZYFA's numerical error is within a few percent of that of Composable Kernel and Triton and 62-78% lower than that of AITER's. The source code is available at https://github.com/Zyphra/zyfa.

title: Information Games: Strategic Crowding and Firm Repositioning in Language-Model Space
abstract: When firms respond to new market opportunities, their capacity choices alter the future discounted free cash flows available to both competitors and investors. In competitive markets, these investment decisions publicized in news articles and analyst reports, measuring the changes in capital structure, product mix, firm leadership, risk exposure and operating procedure made by the firm. Modern search engines rely on Large Language Models to measure the relevancy of source documents to given search query. These measurements let researchers represent these news articles as clouds of dense vectors whose information geometry reflects the dissimilarity of firms over time. Building on Xu et al. (2022), we develop a model of costly competitive adjustment in which firms allocate capacity in which firms make firm capacity adjustment towards free cash flow shocks. Using a novel sandwich estimator, we analyse the sign and magnitude of this predicted adjustment using multi-agent simulation, and validate our findings on a sample of news and analyst reports from Nasdaq-listed companies between 2018-2022.

title: SoK: The Security-Safety Continuum of Multimodal Foundation Models
abstract: Multimodal foundation models (MFMs) integrate diverse data modalities to support complex and wide-ranging tasks. However, this integration also introduces distinct safety and security challenges. In this paper, we unify the concepts of safety and security in the context of MFMs by identifying critical threats that arise from both model behavior and system-level interactions. We propose a taxonomy grounded in information theory, evaluating risks through the concepts of channel capacity, signal, noise, and bandwidth. This perspective provides a principled way to analyze how information flows through MFMs and how vulnerabilities can emerge across modalities. Building on this foundation, we introduce a deterministic minimax formulation to analyze defense mechanisms and to study a structural asymmetry of defense in multimodal systems. Our analysis indicates that model-centric defenses, which primarily operate by suppressing noise or enhancing signal, tend to exhibit diminishing effectiveness against increasingly adaptive attacks. In contrast, system-level safeguards that constrain authorized information flow and agent behavior impose stronger limits on adversarial impact by reducing effective bandwidth. To operationalize this insight, our framework maps attacks and defenses onto information-theoretic axes, effectively organizing and reducing the defense search space. Using a proposed Defense Coverage Index (DCI) to evaluate 15 representative defenses, we observe that system-level bandwidth constraints provide stronger and more consistent protection across attack classes than brittle model-level mechanisms. Finally, we formalize an MFM ``self-destruction threshold'' that specifies when termination should be triggered, offering a concrete activation rule for circuit-breaker safeguards in multimodal systems.

title: Structured variation in daily life experience within and across individuals.
abstract: Human experience varies across contexts and individuals. Yet, psychological studies typically seek to constrain rather than discover structured variation. Here we leverage a powerful alternative approach to examine variability in emotional experience by sampling multimodally from individuals across a variety of contexts throughout their daily life and employing unsupervised machine learning to discover reliable, person-specific, multimodal patterns of experience. Healthy adults (N=97) completed 14 days of biologically-triggered experience sampling. Participants wore mobile cardiac monitors for 8 hours/day and reported their current valence, arousal, primary activity (e.g., relaxing), social context (e.g., alone), and emotional experience (via free report) when prompted. Prompts were initiated whenever a sustained change in cardiac activity (i.e., interbeat interval) was detected in the absence of gross bodily movements (and twice randomly each day). From each event (10,755 total, M=110.9 events/person), we extracted cardiovascular, postural, affective, and contextual features, which were submitted to integrative clustering to derive reliable patterns for each individual. Integrative clustering identified 313 multimodal patterns (M=3.2 patterns/person). The number of multimodal patterns varied across people, as did, to varying extents, their nature. The features that best distinguished patterns from one another also varied by person. Critically, all participants mapped many emotion labels to a single multimodal pattern, and a single emotion label to many patterns (i.e., a many-to-many mapping). Our comprehensive approach has broad utility for discovering structured variation in emotional experience ‘in the wild’ and provides further evidence that emotions are diverse populations of instances constructed by a perceiver in context.

title: Beyond Hash Matching: AI-Based Detection of Previously Unidentified CSAM and its Legal Implications in the EU
abstract: The detection of previously unidentified Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) remains a significant challenge for law enforcement authorities, online service providers, and child protection organizations, as traditional hash-matching technologies are primarily designed to identify previously verified material. This paper reviews and classifies existing AI-based technologies that could complement hash-based approaches and support the detection, analysis, and prioritization of potentially harmful content. The reviewed approaches are organized into three categories: real-time image and video analysis, image and video classification and tagging, and AI-based behavioral monitoring. A comparative analysis examines the capabilities, limitations, and potential integration of general-purpose computer vision platforms, content moderation services, and specialized CSAM detection tools within existing detection workflows. An experimental evaluation was conducted using Google Cloud Vision AI and Sightengine to investigate sexual-content classification and child-adult age estimation. The results highlight differences in classification taxonomies and outputs across providers, as well as significant limitations in age classification, particularly for adolescents. These findings highlight the importance of using AI-based assessments as complementary tools for analysis and prioritization, rather than as definitive determination of CSAM. Finally, the paper examines the relevant European Union regulatory framework, with particular attention to the EU AI Act, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), fundamental rights, transparency, accountability, and human oversight. The legal analysis highlights how regulatory obligations and safeguards may differ depending on the deployment context, potentially creating inconsistencies across interconnected detection and reporting workflows.

title: Random Symbolic Boosting: A Geometric Approach to Symbolic Regression
abstract: Symbolic models offer interpretability, but their construction through generational evolution can be computationally expensive. This article presents Random Symbolic Boosting (RSB), a method that constructs explicit additive symbolic models via boosting over populations of randomly generated syntax trees, eliminating the need for generational evolution. The idea combines two observations: high-dimensional spaces can be spanned by enough linearly independent vectors, and the semantics of syntax trees can be directly manipulated as such vectors. It is shown that, for Ordinary Least Squares, the boosting process guarantees a monotonic reduction of the training error for both regression and classification. Furthermore, an adaptive geometric early stopping mechanism is introduced. It is based on the angle between the prediction and target vectors, is independent of the problems scale, and requires no adjustments across tasks. Evaluated on a standard benchmark for symbolic regression, the method is located at the Pareto-optimal point between predictive accuracy and training time, ranking first on the real-world datasets. Additionally, it was tested on a large tabular classification benchmark with 200 problems, achieving competitive results.

title: SpecCTMC: Exact Speculative Simulation of Diffusion Language Model Continuous-Time Markov Chains
abstract: Masked diffusion language models offer parallel text generation, but independently sampling multiple tokens can disrupt their dependencies and change the output distribution. Exact continuous-time sampling avoids this approximation, yet typically requires one sequential model evaluation per token. We introduce SpecCTMC, a training-free speculative sampler that reduces this sequential bottleneck without a separate draft model. SpecCTMC proposes successive token updates using previously computed model predictions, evaluates their intermediate states in parallel, and applies an exact acceptance-and-correction procedure. We prove that SpecCTMC preserves the joint distribution of event times, generation order, and token values of the underlying continuous-time Markov chain. It therefore introduces neither time-discretization error nor additional factorization error from parallel decoding. Experiments on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-v0-Instruct-7B across five benchmarks demonstrate 1.73-4.38x fewer sequential model evaluations than direct continuous-time sampling, while preserving the reference sampling distribution. Our code is available at: https://github.com/kasakh/specctmc

title: Should We Pay This Much for Robustness? Efficient Proxy Certificates with Marginal Guarantees
abstract: Modern classifiers remain sensitive to small input perturbations, while strong model-agnostic robustness certificates such as randomized smoothing are often too expensive for deployment, requiring an extensive number (e.g. 2000) of model forward passes per input. We propose a framework that delegates certification to a cheap proxy function while statistically controlling its deviation from the original sound certificate. Given an exchangeable unlabeled calibration set, we tune the proxy via robust conformal risk control to guarantee a bounded marginal (rather than pointwise) false-approval rate: the probability, over future inputs, that the proxy accepts an input whose prediction is flipped due to perturbation. The resulting proxy certificate can be used either as a standalone marginal certificate or as a fallback mechanism that invokes the expensive certificate only when the proxy rejects. We provide both single-sample and sample-heavy calibration recipes. Empirically, as a standalone certificate our method reduces the test-time certification cost to a single model forward while retaining much of the certified performance of randomized smoothing at small radii, and as a fallback it recovers the certified ratio of randomized smoothing at a more modest speedup. This enables cheap yet effective robustness guarantees for larger architectures such as vision transformers and language models.

title: Learning Multi-Agent Orchestration:Higher-Order Interactions in Policy Improvement
abstract: Learned orchestration has emerged as a promising paradigm for large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems, in which a central orchestrator selects agents and controls the information they receive throughout a task. Despite rapid empirical progress, existing methods train the orchestrator by crediting each decision with its own advantage, implicitly assuming that the other decisions in the episode stay fixed. This assumption fails in orchestration, where the contribution of each decision to the final outcome depends on the decisions preceding it, so the gain of a joint update is not the sum of its per-decision effects. To address this challenge, we introduce \textbf{IAPO}, an interaction-aware policy optimization framework that explicitly accounts for interactions among decisions. Specifically, IAPO exactly decomposes the performance difference between two policies into the effects of individual decisions and their interactions, which we prove can account for half of the attainable gain, and then optimizes both from sampled trajectories while certifying that every update is an improvement. On long-input versions of GSM8K, MATH, DROP, MBPP and HumanEval, against fifteen published multi-agent and workflow-search systems on the same 7B executor, IAPO's deployed plans reach the strongest system's accuracy with fewer tokens, and removing the interaction term costs 7 to 17 points of accuracy on code.

title: Cybersecurity Risks in Safety-Critical Off-Highway Vehicle Controllers and Hardware Security Modules-Backed Mitigation Strategies
abstract: Off-highway vehicles (OHV) increasingly rely on electronically controlled, safety-critical systems such as braking, steering, powertrain, and implement control electronic control unit (ECUs). The integration of connectivity, telematics, precision-agriculture features, and semi-autonomous operation has transformed these machines into complex cyber-physical systems. While these capabilities improve productivity and operational efficiency, they also expand the attack surface, creating cybersecurity risks that can directly impact vehicle control, operator safety, and field operations. Off-highway platforms often operate in remote environments, use legacy in-vehicle networks, and have long service lifecycles, further amplifying exposure to cyber threats. Recent research and real-world demonstrations highlight that many attacks on safety-critical controllers exploit fundamental architectural weaknesses rather than advanced exploits. Common scenarios include unauthenticated CAN-based communication enabling message injection, replay, or spoofing of steering and braking commands; compromised telematics or wireless interfaces pivoting into safety-critical networks; unsecure over-the-air update mechanisms permitting unauthorized firmware installation; and misuse of diagnostic or maintenance access paths to invoke privileged ECU functions. Network-level attacks such as denial-of-service and sensor-level manipulation, including GPS or perception spoofing, further threaten the integrity and availability of control functions relied upon by modern agricultural machines. This paper examines these attack scenarios in the context of off-highway safety-critical controllers and discusses how Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) provide a practical trust anchor for mitigating such risks. HSMs onboard hardware-isolated execution, tamper-resistant key storage, and cryptographic enforcement that strengthen ECU security beyond secure boot. HSM-backed mechanisms enable authenticated and integrity-protected software updates, prevent execution of unauthorized firmware, support message authentication and freshness on in-vehicle networks, and harden diagnostic access through secure challenge-response mechanisms. By grounding cybersecurity risks in realistic off-highway use cases and mapping them to deployable HSM-backed controls, the paper illustrates how hardware-anchored security enhances runtime trust, supports safety objectives, and aligns off-highway vehicle architectures with emerging vehicle cybersecurity expectations, including the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). In addition, a PoC implementation based on an automotive-grade embedded controller is presented to demonstrate secure boot, authenticated CAN communication, diagnostic access control, and runtime integrity monitoring, together with a validation methodology that demonstrates their practical effectiveness.

title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
abstract: Large language models have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet they remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks that circumvent safety mechanisms and elicit harmful or unintended outputs. Although safety can be improved through model fine-tuning, such approaches can be computationally expensive and may degrade previously acquired capabilities through catastrophic forgetting. Recent jailbreak defenses have therefore explored targeted interventions on specific model components associated with unsafe behavior. However, existing approaches typically decouple two inherently related decisions: where to intervene and how to modify the selected components. Such sequential optimization may be suboptimal because the optimal intervention location can depend on the intervention applied there, and vice versa. In this work, we introduce AttentionSwitch, the first jailbreak defense to jointly optimize intervention sites and strengths within a frozen LLM. Specifically, AttentionSwitch learns a sparse set of attention heads together with query-conditioned multiplicative scaling factors, allowing the outputs of the selected heads to be either attenuated or amplified without altering the directions of their representations. Across popular language models and jailbreak attacks, AttentionSwitch outperforms existing defenses, with particularly strong results when training data is scarce.

title: Reproducing Kernel (Quasi-)Banach Spaces with the $\ell^p$ Coefficient Norms
abstract: This paper advances the theory of reproducing kernel Banach spaces (RKBSs) by investigating the general $\ell^p$ regularization framework, with a particular focus on the non-convex regime $0<p<1$. While our preceding work established the foundation for RKBSs with the $\ell^1$ norm, the pursuit of stronger sparsity---closer to the $\ell^0$ pseudo-norm---naturally motivates this exploration into $\ell^p$ quasi-norms. For $0<p<1$, we construct reproducing kernel quasi-Banach spaces (RKQBSs) with $\ell^p$ quasi-norms and establish existence and sparsity results for interpolation and regularized learning under appropriate assumptions. We characterize the linear and relaxed representer theorems in terms of a generalized Lebesgue constant and derive bounds under kernel decay, sample spacing, and stability assumptions. For $p>1$, we construct RKBSs using a fixed countable dictionary, establish minimizer existence, and identify the optimal relaxed representer factor through an off-sample coefficient operator. These results reveal fundamental differences between the regimes $0<p<1$, $p=1$, and $p>1$. Numerical experiments compare the accuracy and sparsity of solutions for these three cases.
